newsitem.title: UK: P&O confident of addressing EU merger concern.
newsitem.headline: P&O confident of addressing EU merger concern.

text.p: British ferry giant Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc (P&O) said on Wednesday it was confident of meeting the European Union's concerns about its planned merger with Stena Line of Sweden.

Earlier on Wednesday Stena confirmed the EU had sent a "letter of serious doubts" about the merger to both companies. But Lord Sterling, P&O chairman, said in a statement "We have been keeping in close touch with Commission officials and this is very much what we expected. I am confident we will be able to meet the points they have raised."
P&O echoed a statement from Stena that it hoped to receive a "letter of comfort" from the Commission by early July. This would formally conclude the EU's review of the merger.

P&O's statement said that the Commission had essentially accepted the merger arguments for the freight market, which will see intense competition. But it is more concerned about the short sea tourist market, which could see an eventual duopoly of Eurotunnel Plc's Channel Tunnel services and those from P&O Stena Line.
The Commission wanted to examine the need to keep the operations of the merged company separate from the operations of the parent groups, said P&O.

Peter Smith, director of corporate affairs at P&O summed up the position. "This effectively clears the freight side of the merger. On the tourist side, this (Commission concern) doesn't prevent us from still making major savings," he told Reuters.

The Commission will be examining issues like how the tourist services are promoted and sold in brochures. "These are important issues for the regulator to be clear about. But on the commercial side of the merger it would have little impact," said Smith.

"There will be no significant impact on cost savings and we are still looking at finding 75 million stg in savings on an annualised basis. We are sticking very strongly to that figure," he told Reuters.
